 Dated this the 10th day of October, 2024  ORDER Petitioners claimed to be accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.298 of 2024 of Neyyattinkara Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram.

However, the learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions submitted that the 4 th petitioner is the first accused while petitioners 2, 3 and 4 are the remaining accused out of a total of five accused in the crime.

sentences.text:
According to the prosecution, the accused had with an intention to defraud the defacto complainant promised him a loan after calling him through WhatsApp and made him believe that it is from the Union Bank and thereafter collected an amount of Rs.49,810/- on different dates for the purpose of the loan and later failed to disburse the loan or return the money and thereby committed the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3.

Though an affidavit projecting the settlement arrived at between the parties have been produced,
on a perusal of the nature of allegations in the FIR, this Court notices that an online fraud has been allegedly committed by the accused.

4. Having regard to the increase in online frauds in the country and the public interest involved in curbing such offences, the settlement CRL.MC NO. 7769 OF 2024 2024:KER:75244 between the defacto complainant and the accused by itself is not sufficient to quash the proceedings, especially at the investigation stage.

5. In the decision in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303], the Supreme Court had observed that though cases can be quashed on the basis of settlement arrived at between the parties, the same ought to be exercised bearing in mind the public interest involved.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since there is a public interest in preventing online frauds, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to quash the proceedings on the basis of settlement.

Accordingly, I dismiss this Crl.M.C. Sd/-
